philosophy.title: One operator. Four companies. One standard.
philosophy.lede: A holding only earns the name when it runs what it owns.

principles.title: Build, don't resell.
principles.body: Every subsidiary is built and run to the same engineering standard. No outsourced core, no white-labelled product — the hard parts are ours.

principles.title: Bits and material.
principles.body: Operating-system kernels and autonomous agents on one side, furniture and architecture on the other. We build the hard things — whether they ship in code or in material.

principles.title: Honesty over hype.
principles.body: Our AI agents reason inside sandboxes and self-debug under a microscope. We build for verifiable truth, not for demos.

items.body: We fund the companies we run — capital aligned to engineering, not to a pitch deck.
Kernels, agents, dashboards, and the furniture and rooms around them — built to one standard, ours.
We don't flip what we build. We run our companies for the long term.

cta.title: Building something hard?

about.title: I'm Daniel Limón.
about.lede: An engineer who decided to run what he builds. Because people deserve the best.
about.body1: I am an operator and builder based in Mexico. My journey began the moment my mother showed me how to draw with Python’s Turtle library, seeing code translate into physical shapes on a screen instantly captivated me. By the time I was six years old, I had immersed myself in web technologies, mastering HTML, CSS, and JavaScript by age nine and picking up various certifications purely out of curiosity and boredom. I work on almost all the hard things you can imagine, from operating-system to an studio that builds the furniture and architecture around them. I don't buy equity in other people's companies and I don't relabel other people's work, if my name is on it, I built it and I operate it.
about.body2: Programming quickly became my ultimate playground. I began building toy operating systems in HTML as a hobby, iterating through early projects like RedOS, PixelOS, mokeOS, and ShimmerOS. That early experimentation laid the foundation for my current bare-metal operating system, Galileo. When the AI boom emerged with ChatGPT, I was determined to train my own LLMs Google Colab to engineer around local hardware constraints. I think a holding only earns the name when it runs what it owns. So that's what this is: one operator, four companies, held to one standard. Not flipped, not resold, not pitched to a deck.
about.body3: Driven by an instinct to craft systems from the ground up, my work expanded in 2025 into real estate, construction, architectural design, interior design, and furniture crafting, sparked by the encouragement of my godfather, Sinesio René Hernández.
about.body4: I work on almost all the hard things you can imagine, from low-level operating systems to the studio that builds the furniture and architecture around them. I don't buy equity in other people's companies, and I don't relabel other people's work: if my name is on it, I built it and I operate it.
about.body5: I believe a holding only earns the name when it runs what it owns. So that is what this is: one operator, four companies, held to one standard. Not flipped, not resold, and not pitched to a deck.
about.body6: I fund the companies I run, I ship the parts that are hardest, and I stay on them. Capital is strictly aligned to engineering, not to a pitch. The hard parts are mine; the long term is the point.
